question: Bind — ATK, spike planted A (Reactor), 3v1 up, 23s on defuse. You hold near A Site with an ally; the single surviving defender is somewhere off-site. How do you close the post-plant?

options.label: Hold crossfire angles on the spike and let the clock run — force the lone defender into two guns to even try a defuse
options.explication_courte: You're 3v1 with the spike down and 23s — time is entirely on your side. Set a crossfire covering the plant so the lone defender has to show himself to defuse and dies to the first gun. You never need to move.

sources_option.citation: Post-plant is about holding angles that cover the spike and letting the clock work; make the defender expose himself rather than hunting him

options.label: Push out together to hunt down the last defender and guarantee the kill
options.explication_courte: Chasing a lone defender off-site with the spike already down throws your whole advantage — you leave the plant unwatched, expose yourselves to his held angle, and give him the isolated 1v1s he needs. Time already wins this for you.

sources_option.citation: With a numbers and time advantage, value staying alive over extra kills; chasing the last defender risks giving the trade back

options.label: Split apart to cover two separate entrances to site so he can't sneak in
options.explication_courte: Covering both entries is reasonable with the man-advantage, but spreading too thin turns your crossfire into two isolated 1v1s; a good defender picks one, wins it, and now it's a 2v1 with the plant contested. Keep the guns mutually supporting.

sources_option.citation: Cover the common defuse approaches, but keep positions mutually supporting so the defender can't isolate a single gun

options.label: Both hide off the spike and let him start the defuse, planning to swing on the defuse sound
options.explication_courte: Ceding vision of the spike to bait a defuse is a coinflip you don't need in a 3v1 — a fake defuse, a quick tap-defuse, or a util-cover defuse can steal the round outright. With this much advantage you never give up eyes on the bomb.

sources_option.citation: Never fully cede vision of the spike when you can hold it; fake defuses and util-covered defuses punish attackers who give up eyes on the bomb

explication_longue: A 3v1 post-plant with 23 seconds on the clock is close to a free round, and the only way to lose it is to over-play. The spike is down at A (Reactor), the clock is running for you, and the last defender must come to the bomb — so the correct play is to set a crossfire that covers the plant and simply wait. To even attempt a defuse he has to expose himself to at least one of your guns while stationary on the spike; against two mutually supporting angles that is suicide. Chasing him off-site inverts everything: you abandon eyes on the bomb, walk into whatever angle he's holding, and hand him the isolated duels a lone defender lives for — all to secure a kill the clock was already going to hand you. Splitting to cover both entrances is defensible but must not become two lone 1v1s; keep the guns close enough to trade. And baiting the defuse — hiding off the spike to swing on the sound — is a needless coinflip in a 3v1: fake defuses, half-defuses, and util-covered defuses all exist to punish attackers who give up vision. Hold the crossfire, watch the spike, let time close the round.

sources.citation: Hold angles covering the spike, keep positions mutually supporting, and let the defuse clock force the defender to expose himself
